verdict.rationale: Skyvern's docs describe saving a login once and having it reused by every agent. Skyvern itself fills the username, password and 2FA code, and the model gets placeholders instead of the real values. It supports TOTP, email and SMS codes, and integrates with Bitwarden, 1Password and Azure Key Vault. The community comment about plain-text credentials is general worry, not concrete contradicting evidence, so it does not create a dispute. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that vault-backed TOTP logins work without exposing secrets to the model.

support.subject: As an automation-engineer, I can store credentials in a vault and have the agent complete logins including TOTP/2FA challenges without exposing secrets to the model

citations.quote: Save a login once and every agent can use it. Skyvern fills the username, password and 2FA code into the page for you. The model that drives the browser gets placeholders, not your values.
Skyvern handles logins with stored credentials, TOTP/authenticator codes, email and SMS verification, magic links, and password manager integrations with Bitwarden, 1Password, and Azure Key Vault.
Skyvern handles authentication end-to-end, from simple passwords to multi-factor flows with TOTP codes, email verification, and magic links.
